code_rust_review.scope: Changed production, explicit Mode9 dispatch, client APIs, receiver admission/cache integration, tests, three-arm harness, workflow and supervisor; comparison against baseline3fd3199 and committed design.
checked: Whole codec shares exact configured encoder parameters and validates a single checksummed content-size-bound frame before bounded allocation; exact output identity remains mandatory before publication.

Immutable private prepared payload retains the selected encoding; Raw/Whole/Schema strict comparison preserves tie order, cold raw seed is charged, target length and batch limits are checked, and no send-time recompression is introduced.

Whole mode forbids base/manifest; prepared receiver state stays namespace/mode scoped with bounded opt-in retention, shared-quota admission and existing authentication/publication behavior. Existing adaptive candidate eligibility is unchanged.

Harness times outer selection/encode through commit ACK, including any lazy seed once; context construction and forced upfront seed enter session totals. Candidate receipts are checked against actual forced-arm bodies and stopped-store exact readback joins.

Same executable/configuration for all three arms, registered distinct targets and balanced order, fixed source/attempt gates, secret scoped to transfer step, fresh receiver ownership, sequential no-retry collection, and always-retained failure artifacts.

Eight new production tests cover exact data/zero/size limits, strict cost tie, genuine paid schema seed, scoped cache reuse, corruption/recovery and missing-base rejection; harness real31-object qualification and negative receipt fixtures remain separate from performance results.
limitations: Review is scoped to this change, not whole-project formal verification.
Readiness is caller knowledge and cannot authorize an object; missing or revoked state fails without a retry/reoffer.
Selection minimizes this transfer successful-miss HTTP-body cost, not total packet traffic, CPU, elapsed time or future globally optimal seed placement.
Encoder selection computes both candidates; any CPU or WAN speed benefit is unmeasured at this gate. Receiver CPU is handler-only and exchange wall includes remote work/waiting.
Current coverage is focused lines/functions, with no branch or MC/DC claim.
